enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
510 PM MDT Tue Oct 20 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 530 PM MDT Tue Oct 20 2026

 - Isolated showers and thunderstorms this evening, mostly 
   limited to Southwest New Mexico. A few storms may be strong to 
   severe.

 - Warm temperatures over the next couple days, with lowland 
   highs in the lower 80s. This is slightly above normal for late 
   October.

 - Widespread chances for showers and thunderstorms return 
   Thursday and Friday as moisture moves north into the region. 
   Some stronger storms could result in localized flooding, 
   damaging winds, and large hail.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1200 PM MDT Tue Oct 20 2026

A large upper trough will continue spinning away off the coast of
California. Meanwhile an upper high is to our southeast. This 
will focus moisture and chances for storms over AZ and our western
portions of the CWA Wednesday. A Marginal Risk is out tomorrow 
highlighting the Continental Divide and west for strong storms 
that could produce severe hail and severe wind gusts. The 
aforementioned trough lifts out over the Lower CO Basin Thursday 
but this will spell a very active couple days for the area with 
potential for flooding, and strong storms that could produce hail 
and severe wind gusts. Abnormally moist conditions on the way 
Thursday where PWs will reach up to 1.1" to 1.2" which is record 
breaking, or at least near record breaking, which will add to the 
flooding threat.

Behind the main aforementioned trough, another low cuts off and 
gives us a little more energy for Saturdays storms. Continued rain
and thunderstorm chances Saturday where severe thunderstorms are 
possible once again, as well as flooding. By the end of the 
weekend, this trough finally gets sucked into the main flow 
allowing some drier and clearing conditions from west to east. 
Another strong cold front possible Monday into Tuesday with windy 
conditions. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 530 PM MDT Tue Oct 20 2026

VMC through forecast period with skies FEW-SCT080, SCT-BKN250 
this evening. Isolated TS across SW NM, not expected to affect 
local terminals. Dry weather overnight with increasing high cirrus
coverage. Surface winds generally 040-080 AOB 5 knots tonight, 
then increasing out of the SE 110-140 at 5 to 10 knots Wednesday 
afternoon.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1200 PM MDT Tue Oct 20 2026

Low fire weather concerns through the week ahead as min RHs stay 
above critical thresholds and 20 foot winds stay 5-10 mph each 
afternoon. Min RH values across the lowlands will be 30-50% each 
afternoon through Sunday, increasing to 50-70% Monday and Tuesday.
Min RHs will be anywhere from 40-80% in the area mountains each 
day through Tuesday. Continued rain chances each day. Storm 
coverage will be over the Gila region and far western NM locations
tomorrow, some storms may become strong. Thursday and Friday will
feature strong thunderstorms that could produce hail, damaging 
wind gusts, and flash flooding. Storm coverage is areawide 
Thursday and into Friday. Storms will focus across much of the 
area except for far western NM over the weekend. Some storms may 
become strong to severe. 

&&
